actions.description: Receive Stephanie Morris's call about the valuation fee and the property disposition direction. Pay her $1,500 valuation fee as committed at tick 10 — a professional obligation I named explicitly and must close. In the same call, give her a clear answer on direction: the quiet logistics buyer inquiry has been running 30 days. Ask her directly for a preliminary read — has she contacted any logistics or delivery operator buyers? What early signal, if any, has she gotten? If she reports zero traction, I tell her to focus the next 30 days specifically on EV fleet servicing operators and last-mile delivery consolidators — these are the buyers the RoboRide residential expansion is creating in real time. I keep the $300K floor. I do not lower it yet.
actions.expected_outcome: Valuation fee paid, closing the professional obligation. Buyer inquiry status clarified. Direction confirmed: if no signal at day 60, I reactivate the Kevin O'Brien EV charger loan and proceed with retrofit-and-hold.

actions.description: Contact Priya Sharma by phone and request a business insurance quote — specifically business interruption coverage and property liability for the gas station. This has been named as a deferred failure in my tick 6 and tick 9 reflections. I have four dependents and no coverage on a business in structural decline. I call Priya, explain I am a neighbor who needs a real quote, not a generic product push, and ask her to walk me through what coverage would cost for a small fuel retail business. I tell her my situation honestly: revenue is declining, I am evaluating a possible property sale, and I want to understand what adequate coverage looks like for the next 6-12 months regardless of which path I choose.
actions.expected_outcome: Receive a real business insurance quote from Priya. Eliminate the unmitigated coverage risk I have been carrying for 11 ticks with four dependents. Establish a professional relationship with Priya that may develop into a policy purchase.

actions.description: Follow up with Maria Santos's office or the Millfield Chamber of Commerce to determine the definitive status of the tick 2 small business stabilization grant application. Nine ticks have passed with no outcome notification. I contact the Chamber by phone, reference my application date and business name, and ask for a status. If the application is in a backlog, I name the financial pressure directly: savings are down significantly since application, and the grant would materially affect my decision between a property sale and an EV retrofit investment. I am not hostile. I am specific and persistent.
actions.expected_outcome: Definitive answer on grant status — awarded, denied, or pending with a timeline. If awarded, document the $5,000 income. If denied, document the reason and assess whether a policy appeal is available. Either way, close this as an open thread.

actions.description: Attend Lisa Freeman's Financial Triage Navigator session at the community center. I have heard about this through word-of-mouth and it is directly relevant: I am a small business owner at L1 with a 60-day decision gate approaching and no insurance coverage. I go not as someone in crisis but as someone who wants to understand what resources exist for business owners navigating the same structural disruption I am in. I also go because Kevin O'Brien's office hours are reportedly running there — and I need to stay current on what the bank is offering for small business owners in my situation. My $12K EV charger loan application is sitting in that pipeline.
actions.expected_outcome: Better understanding of available community resources and the Financial Triage Navigator infrastructure Lisa Freeman has built. Possible reconnection with Kevin O'Brien on the status of the paused EV charger loan and what the portfolio expansion decision means for my application.

reasoning: Tick 11 is a convergence tick for Amir Patel. The 60-day logistics buyer inquiry is approaching its midpoint and Stephanie is calling to confirm the valuation fee and ask for direction. I must pay that fee — it is a professional obligation I named explicitly.
